comments.body:
# PHASE 1 COMPLETE — root cause PROVEN at runtime (rebar-debug protocol)

Three independent mechanisms, each confirmed by a driven experiment against a REAL rejected
push (a local bare origin whose `pre-receive` hook exits 1 with GH013-shaped stderr), not by
mocks. Reproduced independently twice (orchestrator + a blind investigator subagent).

## The contract this violates

`docs/concurrency.md:296-299` (verbatim): "Push is **best-effort**: a failed push ... never
fails the caller — it **warns**, leaves local commits intact, and the branch stays diverged.
`rebar fsck` surfaces that divergence as a `PUSH_PENDING` notice ... **so it is not silent**."
`docs/concurrency.md:288-292`: every write propagates "**immediately**".

So "never fails the caller" IS authoritative intent and must be preserved — the remedy is a
SIGNAL, never an exception. "not silent" is the half that is false today.

## RC-1 — the rejection reason is captured and then thrown away (PRIMARY)

`src/rebar/_store/push.py:27`
    _NON_FF = re.compile(r"non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first", re.IGNORECASE)

This regex is the sole classifier splitting "retriable non-fast-forward" from "terminal,
report-with-stderr". Git's line for a policy/push-protection decline is
`! [remote rejected] HEAD -> tickets (pre-receive hook declined)` — it contains the bare
substring `rejected`. So at `push.py:175` `if not _NON_FF.search(stderr)` is FALSE, the ONLY
stderr-bearing log call (`push.py:176`) is skipped, and control falls into three futile
fetch+merge+retry cycles before exiting at `push.py:296`:

    logger.warning("tickets branch push failed after %s retries", _MAX_RETRIES)

which interpolates only the retry count. `run_git` DID capture the GH013 body
(`gitutil.py:57-97`, `capture_output=True`; present in `res.stderr` at `push.py:174`) — it is
destroyed inside the process that held it. The outage therefore reads as transient contention.

### Measured (REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always, the default)

    $ rebar comment <id> "an ordinary comment"
    EXIT CODE: 0
    STDOUT:    (empty)
    STDERR:    WARNING rebar._store.push: tickets branch push failed after 3 retries
    origin/tickets..HEAD: 1     (second identical write -> 2)

    $ git push origin HEAD:tickets     # what the agent had to run MANUALLY
    remote: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/tickets.
    remote: - Push cannot contain secrets
    remote:   locations: - commit: 0a09e51c9f  path: 129e-.../xxx-COMMENT.json:1
     ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> tickets (pre-receive hook declined)

### The discriminating control (this is what rules out "the reason was never captured")

A push failure whose stderr contains NO non-ff token (remote URL pointed at a nonexistent
repo) DOES take `push.py:176` and prints the full reason:

    WARNING rebar._store.push: tickets branch push failed (exit 128): fatal: '...nonexistent.git'
    does not appear to be a git repository ...

So the reason-bearing branch works perfectly. The REJECTED class specifically routes past it.
Direct check: `_NON_FF.search(<real GH013 stderr>)` -> True, matching on the token `rejected`.

### This exact bug class was already fixed once, elsewhere in this repo

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:723-747` (bug 4afc) carries the identical
finding in its own comment: "only `stale info` is the --force-with-lease signal; `rejected`
and `cannot lock ref` also cover hook declines, rate limits, server errors ... which are not
lease movement", and fixes it with `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS = ("file exists", "hook declined",
"internal server error", "rate limit")`. Test:
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_push_classification.py`. That is the trusted,
test-backed pattern to model this fix on — `push.py` is the surface that never got the rule.

## RC-2 — the divergence signal is pull-only, so nothing ever re-announces the backlog

`PUSH_PENDING` is computed at exactly one site, `_commands/fsck.py:365` `_tracker_sync_status`,
reachable only from `fsck.py:203` (an explicit `rebar fsck`), and emitted with `is_issue=False`
(`fsck.py:424-429`, pinned by `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_push_pending.py:82`). No write
path consults it: `event_append.py:587` calls `push.push_tickets_branch(canonical)` bare and
returns the COMMIT count; `push_after_commit` (`push.py:299-322`) returns None. The
`push.py:296` warning is byte-identical on write #1 and write #122, so a rejection that
scrolled off screen is unrecoverable context.

Measured: five further writes all exit 0 with the identical one-line message; `show`/`list`/
`ready` print nothing on stderr; ahead-count silently climbed 1 -> 6; only an explicitly
invoked `rebar fsck` named it. THIS is the mechanism that explains eight hours and 122
commits, and "discovered only by a manual git push".

## RC-3 — on three write paths the warning is not merely uninformative, it is undeliverable

- `sync.push = async` (a first-class documented policy value) re-spawns the push as a detached
  `subprocess.Popen(..., stdout=DEVNULL, stderr=DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)`
  (`push.py:128-141`), never waited. The child's warning goes to /dev/null by construction.
  MEASURED: `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=async rebar comment` against the rejecting hook -> exit 0,
  stderr COMPLETELY EMPTY, 1 commit unpushed.
- Library embedders get only the `NullHandler` (`rebar/__init__.py:131`). MEASURED: in-process
  `rebar.comment(...)` -> returned normally, stderr empty.
- Under MCP the handler is installed (`mcp_server.py:688,690`) but targets the SERVER's stderr;
  the writing agent reads only the tool result, and the write tools return no push field.
  (Static evidence only — this limb was not driven end-to-end.)

## Why three causes and not one

RC-1 alone is insufficient — a perfectly worded message still fires once and scrolls away.
RC-2 alone is insufficient — it would not explain the missing GH013 text. RC-3 alone is
insufficient — the foreground CLI case did emit something. Together they completely explain
every observed symptom with nothing residual.

## Test-coverage gap that let this ship

`_NON_FF` appears in NO file under `tests/`. Nothing drives retries-exhausted. The nearest
tests cover only the async spawn-`OSError` branch (`tests/unit/test_push_retry_stash_pop.py:113-123`)
and the LockTimeout case (`:126-149`); `tests/unit/test_store.py:151,156` actively codifies the
silence (`# no raise`, `# no remote -> silent best-effort return`).

## Legitimacy + caller-dependency gates (both cleared)

- RC-1: **defect** — violates the cited `docs/concurrency.md:296-299` "it warns ... so it is
  not silent". RC-2: **incomplete-implementation** — the pull-only detector is the documented
  design, but it never reaches the caller the contract addresses. RC-3: **defect** — on `async`
  the documented "it warns" is false by construction.
- Caller sweep: every caller of `push_tickets_branch`/`push_after_commit` is a bare call whose
  result is discarded (`event_append.py:587,617`; `claim.py:253`; `transition_close.py:462`;
  `compact.py:650,769`; `delete.py:339,399`; `import_ndjson.py:381`), so enriching the warning
  has NO behavioral dependents. One real constraint found: `tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py:198`
  and `tests/integration/test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py:216` assert
  `"failed after 3 retries" not in caplog.text`, so the fix must KEEP that substring and append
  to it rather than reword it (otherwise those negative assertions are silently weakened).

## Scope taken into Phase 2

RC-1 + RC-2 are fixed here: both live on the same failure path in `src/rebar/_store/push.py`.
RC-3 (async DEVNULL / MCP result field / library channel) is a separate architectural change
and is being filed as its own ticket, linked `discovered_from` this one.

# A rejected tickets-branch auto-push fails SILENTLY, and ticket event payloads are never scanned for secrets

Two hardening items carried forward from [rebar:94d0-5d19-2d06-4fa7] (closed). Its incident
(live credentials in a ticket comment) is resolved -- credentials rotated, history scrubbed,
branch pushing again -- but the two conditions that let it run for ~8 hours undetected are
properties of the store, not of that incident, and remain.

## 1. A rejected auto-push is invisible to the agent that wrote

rebar's store auto-commits and auto-pushes every write to `sync.remote`. When that push is
REJECTED, the write still succeeds locally and the command reports success.

Measured during the incident: 122 ticket commits accumulated locally over roughly eight hours
while every push was rejected by GitHub push protection. Every `rebar comment`,
`rebar transition` and `rebar create` in that window returned normally. The divergence was
discovered only because an unrelated CI failure prompted a manual `git push`, which finally
printed the rejection. Consequences observed: a Gerrit change could not pass its ticket gate
because the ticket it referenced existed only locally; evidence recorded on epic children was
invisible to CI and to every other agent session.

The store's whole premise is "every write is shared immediately" (`docs/concurrency.md`). A
push that fails silently breaks that premise while preserving its appearance.

## 2. Ticket event payloads are never scanned for secrets

rebar runs `gitleaks` as its code-review secret gate, but that gate sees CODE. A ticket COMMENT
is the one place an agent routinely pastes raw environment output. Nothing scans it on write.

## PROVEN ROOT CAUSE (rebar-debug Phase 1 complete -- see the RCA comment for full evidence)

Three mechanisms, each confirmed by DRIVING a real rejected push (local bare origin with a
`pre-receive` hook exiting 1 with GH013-shaped stderr), reproduced independently twice.

**RC-1 (primary).** `src/rebar/_store/push.py:27`
`_NON_FF = re.compile(r"non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first", re.IGNORECASE)` is the sole
classifier splitting retriable non-fast-forward from terminal-report-with-stderr. Git's policy
decline line `! [remote rejected] HEAD -> tickets (pre-receive hook declined)` contains the bare
token `rejected`, so `push.py:175` misroutes it onto the retry path, skipping the ONLY
stderr-bearing log call (`push.py:176`), and exits at `push.py:296` with
`"tickets branch push failed after %s retries"` -- retry count only. `run_git` DID capture the
GH013 body (`gitutil.py:57-97`); it is discarded. Control experiment: a failure whose stderr
lacks a non-ff token DOES print the full reason, proving the reason-bearing branch works and
the rejected class specifically routes past it.

**RC-2.** `PUSH_PENDING` is computed at exactly one pull-only site
(`_commands/fsck.py:365` `_tracker_sync_status`, called only from `fsck.py:203`) and is
`is_issue=False` (`fsck.py:424-429`). No write path consults it, so the warning is
byte-identical on write #1 and write #122 and nothing re-announces the growing backlog. This is
the mechanism that explains eight hours.

**RC-3 (split out, see below).** On `sync.push=async` the push is a detached
`Popen(..., stderr=DEVNULL)` (`push.py:128-141`) -- measured: exit 0, stderr COMPLETELY EMPTY.
Library embedders get only the `NullHandler` (`rebar/__init__.py:131`). Under MCP the warning
goes to the server's stderr, never into the tool result the writing agent reads.

**Prior art for the fix.** `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:723-747` (bug 4afc) already
fixed this exact over-broad-`rejected`-substring class, with
`_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS = ("file exists", "hook declined", "internal server error", "rate limit")`
and test `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_push_classification.py`. `push.py` is
the parallel surface that never got the rule.

## FIX PLAN (this ticket)

Scope is RC-1 + RC-2 -- both live on the same failure path in ONE file, `src/rebar/_store/push.py`.

1. Add a policy-rejection classifier beside `_NON_FF`, modelled on the trusted `_ref_lock.py`
   pattern: markers that name a NON-fast-forward cause (`hook declined`, `push declined`,
   `protected branch`, `rate limit`, `internal server error`, `permission denied`, `GH0`) mean
   the rejection is TERMINAL, not retriable. Such a push reports the reason immediately instead
   of burning three futile fetch+merge cycles.
2. Carry the git stderr tail into the terminal retries-exhausted warning at `push.py:296` so
   the failure self-identifies. The substring `failed after 3 retries` MUST be preserved --
   `tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py:198` and
   `tests/integration/test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py:216` assert it is absent in their
   scenarios, and rewording would silently weaken those negative assertions.
3. Include the unpushed-commit count (`origin/tickets..HEAD`) in the failure warning, so every
   subsequent write re-announces an ESCALATING backlog rather than an identical one-shot line.
   This is the "visible N-commits-unpushed state that subsequent commands report" the report
   asks for, and it is what breaks an eight-hour silence.

Constraint held throughout: "never fails the caller" is authoritative intent
(`docs/concurrency.md:296-299`, `push.py:9-11` "ALWAYS returns None",
`tests/unit/test_store.py:151,156`). The remedy is a SIGNAL, never an exception. No caller
signature changes; every caller of `push_tickets_branch`/`push_after_commit` is a bare call
whose result is already discarded, so the change has no behavioral dependents.

Test: a RED-first regression driving a REAL rejected push against a real local bare origin
whose `pre-receive` hook declines -- asserting the surfaced warning names the reason and the
backlog size, and that the write still succeeds. No mocks, no call counts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a rejected auto-push is surfaced to the writing caller rather than failing silently --
      the warning names the git rejection REASON and the number of unpushed commits
- [ ] a test drives a REJECTED push (real git, real pre-receive decline) and asserts the caller
      sees it -- not a mock's call count
- [ ] a policy rejection is not retried three times as if it were a non-fast-forward
- [ ] the best-effort contract is preserved: the write still succeeds and the caller is not
      failed (regression-asserted)
- [ ] a recorded decision on scanning ticket event payloads for secrets on write -- including
      an explicit "no, and here is why" if that is the answer

file_impact.reason: RC-1+RC-2: classify terminal policy rejections; carry the git rejection reason and the unpushed-commit count into the failure warning
RED-first regression driving a real pre-receive decline and asserting the caller sees reason + backlog
